_schema: F4 per-op acceptance policy (DSv4-Flash authored kernels). DRAFT v2 for GPT Astra 6 review + USER ratification. Revised per the F4 design review (reports/kernel-impl-and-provenance_F4_policy_review.md): D1 corrected indexer oracle, D2 removed the unreferenced Sinkhorn invariant, D3 split determinism from oracle bit-exactness, D4 specified tie/metric/precedence semantics. Defines how a kernel output is machine-judged acceptable vs its AUTHORITATIVE oracle. NOT YET ENFORCED. Numerical TOLERANCES and the exact-equality requirement are USER decisions; oracle selection, metric STRUCTURE, and layer-0 gates are the executor proposal and may be implemented before tolerances are set.
status: PROPOSED / UNRATIFIED (v3, D4 clarifications per F4 design review round 2; harness IMPLEMENTED tolerance-independent, 2026-10-09)
gate: F4 (machine-evaluated per-op acceptance policy + fail-closed bench/job exits)
design_principles: ORACLE AUTHORITY FOLLOWS THE PUBLISHED OPERATION, NOT THE CPU BACKEND. The indexer scoring oracle is published model.py Indexer.forward (there is NO indexer primitive in kernel.py, D1); the sparse and Sinkhorn oracles are the published kernel.py primitives; a CPU/FP32 replay is a DIAGNOSTIC PROXY until conformed to the published runtime.

GATE ON THE DECISION THAT MATTERS: for the indexer the gate is the induced TOP-K SELECTION derived FROM THE REFERENCE (not candidate logits); raw-logit error is diagnostic. Whether logits are an ADDITIONAL gate is a user decision.

COSINE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT AND CAN BE UNDEFINED: pair with an explicit per-output max absolute AND relative error (named denominator + near-zero absolute allowance); zero-vector cosine is undefined -> use the absolute check there. Reject non-finite METRICS.

DETERMINISM != ORACLE BIT-EXACTNESS (D3): repeated-run reproducibility, same-path cross-thread equality, and equality-to-a-pinned-oracle are THREE SEPARATE recorded claims. Exact equality to an oracle is a USER choice for a NAMED frozen path (compiler/runtime/backend recorded), not entailed by FP32-scalar.

FINITENESS IS DOMAIN-SPECIFIC (layer 0): legal padding/mask positions carry -inf (compressor overlap padding scores; masked indexer logits); reject NaN/+inf only OUTSIDE the documented supported domain.

FAIL CLOSED: every violation fails BOTH the benchmark AND the job; a nonzero child exit must be propagated to a nonzero job/shell exit (piped logging + final shell commands verified), and a missing oracle / unratified policy / skipped case / exception / NaN-metric must NOT yield a full PASS (layer-0-only runs are labeled PARTIAL).

layer0_hard_gates_tolerance_independent._note: Implementable immediately; needs NO tolerance decision. A layer-0-only run is labeled PARTIAL, not PASS.
gates: output shape + dtype + layout == the declared op contract (int64 fragment vs the caller's int32 conversion kept distinct)

domain-specific finiteness: outputs finite on the documented supported domain; -inf permitted only at legal padding/mask positions; NaN/+inf and invalid indices/scalars OUTSIDE the contract are rejected (reachability/exclusion of all-masked pool softmax is established, not blanket-blessed to zero)
input-domain validation: actual device/dtype/rank/divisibility/scalar-range checked (not assumed covered by F9)
determinism claims recorded SEPARATELY: (a) repeated-run reproducibility, (b) same-path equality across ACTUAL thread counts, (c) [user-optional] equality to a pinned oracle for a NAMED frozen path
complete expected op/path/case inventory present; a missing oracle, skipped case, exception, or NaN metric fails the gate (never a silent PASS)

fail-closed exit: a deliberate failure is exercised through the REAL benchmark and the EXACT job wrapper (piped logging, child failures, final shell commands); child nonzero exit MUST propagate to job nonzero exit

layer1_numerical_vs_oracle._note: Tolerances PROPOSED; user ratifies. Evaluated on normal AND heavy-tailed inputs. ONE explicit per-output predicate (D4 round 2), NOT a silent choice among variants.

metric_predicate.error: e_i = abs(candidate_i - ref_i) per output element
metric_predicate.accept: PROPOSED predicate: e_i <= atol + rtol*abs(ref_i) for EVERY element (combined absolute+relative; atol is the near-zero allowance, rtol the relative slope) AND cosine >= cosine_floor where cosine is DEFINED
metric_predicate.abs_floor: atol doubles as the near-zero switch: when abs(ref_i) <= atol the relative term is dominated by atol (no separate branch needed)
metric_predicate.reduction: per-output / per-row max of e_i (NOT flattened); pre/post/comb evaluated SEPARATELY
metric_predicate.cosine_not_applicable: for either zero-norm vector, cosine is N/A -> use the absolute branch (e_i <= atol) and RECORD cosine=N/A (do NOT evaluate NaN then trip the nonfinite-metric failure)
metric_predicate.masked_domain: validate reference-owned mask/sentinels SEPARATELY; compute e_i/cosine ONLY over the declared finite domain; all-masked rows -> N/A; identical legal -inf values must NOT be subtracted (no NaN)
metric_predicate.nonfinite_metric: an UNEXPECTED nonfinite evaluated metric still FAILS; the N/A exceptions above outrank the generic completeness wording

proposed_bounds_UNRATIFIED.precedence: USER: does a per-path BF16 bound OVERRIDE the global cosine floor? state explicitly

layer2_discrete_selection._note: The downstream decision. Cutoff + gathered scores are derived FROM THE REFERENCE, never candidate logits (D4). Tie rule PROPOSED; user ratifies.
rules: derive the k-th cutoff and gathered scores from the REFERENCE output
require exactly k distinct in-range raw indices; include every score above cutoff + band; exclude every score below cutoff - band; fill remaining slots only from the band

the selected-score MULTISET check is an ALTERNATIVE implementation of the band rule (NOT a second independent gate); its comparison tolerance = the same tie band; it is paired with the raw-index UNIQUENESS guard (scores [2,2,1] k=2: [0,0] is rejected by uniqueness even though its multiset [2,2] == [0,1]'s)
at a -inf cutoff: include ALL finite valid scores, fill the remaining raw slots from legal masked positions, and NEVER subtract infinities (abs(-inf - -inf) is forbidden; use the sentinel branch)

verify the CALLER transformation, not just raw distinctness: valid post-mask ids are unique + correctly offset; repeated -1 is legal; expect k - min(k, valid_count) sentinels when valid scores are finite; keep the int64 fragment distinct from the caller's int32 conversion
k==0 -> validate empty [N,0] int64 and SKIP cutoff/cosine; handle k==S, duplicate scores, invalid k explicitly

published prefill: -inf mask, k=min(512,end_pos//ratio), causally-invalid choices -> -1 + offset only on valid (repeated -1 legal); decode adds offset directly; separate raw distinct indices from post-mask output

set equivalence does NOT establish ordered sparse-kernel numerical equivalence -> ALSO test the composed sparse consumer (reordering changes 64-entry block boundaries + BF16 accumulation); this composed check is ESSENTIAL, not implied by set equality

proposed_UNRATIFIED.note: band width + whether substituting different KV identities is acceptable are USER decisions (equal scores can reference different KV values); any allowed non-tie selection loss is a USER decision

indexer_logits.cpp.oracle: published model.py Indexer.forward scoring stage (lines ~420-432): BF16 einsum score + BF16 ReLU*weights + BF16 reduction boundary, then the TP ALL-REDUCE (line ~423) BEFORE the caller mask/offset. The adapter MUST include the all-reduce, not merely a rank-local scoring oracle. There is NO indexer primitive in kernel.py (D1).
indexer_logits.cpp.diagnostic_only: an FP32 epilogue replay / torch fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch is a DIAGNOSTIC proxy, not the authority
indexer_logits.cpp.gate: the induced top-k SELECTION (layer 2, derived from the reference); raw-logit error is diagnostic (a published-BF16-vs-tiled-FP32 logit difference is NOT evidence the reference is wrong). 511/512 is a MISMATCH under set-match 1.0 unless the differing ids satisfy the ratified tie rule.

indexer_topk.cpp.oracle: torch.topk (published call uses default sorted order; our kernel returns unsorted) -> scope is ORDER-INDEPENDENT membership

compressor.cpp.oracle: intel_cpu_models/dsa_compressor_cpu.py softmax-weighted FP32 pool, AFTER correctly preparing overlap/APE inputs. This covers ONLY the pool stage, NOT the full compressor (state/cast/norm/rotation/quantization remain declared gaps).
compressor.cpp.gate: layer-1 at ALL 3 costed shapes (R=128/D=512, R=8/D=512, R=8/D=128), masked/overlap states (leading -inf padding) included; bit-exact only if the user freezes the path

sparse_attend.cpp.oracle_serving: published kernel.py sparse_attn BF16 primitive (lines ~294-350): BF16 tensors + intermediate-probability cast of blockwise UNNORMALIZED exponentials + sink + BF16 output. Authority for BOTH candidate paths.
sparse_attend.cpp.oracle_diagnostic: bench_sparse_attend.py inline FP32 reference (has the sink, but is PRE-GATHERED and LACKS the BF16 unnormalized-exp cast) -> scalar-math diagnostic only; do NOT use the stale no-sink module oracle
sparse_attend.cpp.gate: layer-1 vs the BF16 primitive for serving equivalence; evaluate the full window+compressed path (see shape_coverage), not only K=512 pre-gathered

sinkhorn.cpp.oracle: pin + independently conform the SGLang _hc_split_sinkhorn_torch helper to the published kernel.py recurrence (eps placements ~391-423, defaults ~430, hc_mult=4, iters=20, eps=1e-6, pre/post transforms). Its import name alone is NOT authority.
sinkhorn.cpp.gate: layer-1 cosine + abs/rel on ALL THREE outputs (pre/post/comb) vs the conformed recurrence. NO universal doubly-stochastic row/col-sum bound (D2: the finite 20-iteration eps-regularized algorithm does NOT converge to 1e-5 — counterexample E1 exceeds it ~2400x); report convergence residuals SEPARATELY as diagnostics; keep the algorithm eps 1e-6 DISTINCT from any acceptance tolerance

combine.cpp.oracle: published model.py Block.hc_pre: multiply then torch.sum, then a dtype cast. The local einsum is mathematically equivalent but is NOT an established bit-exact oracle.
combine.cpp.gate: layer-1 cosine + abs/rel; bit-exact only if the user freezes the path (FMA/reduction order need not match torch bits)

shape_coverage_required._note: A machine-enumerated case manifest with source/CAPTURE identity (dims, strides, dtypes, backend, phase, batch, TP, mask/state) — naming the shapes in prose is intent only.
shape_coverage_required.compressor_note: ratio==4 => coff=2 => an 8-token overlapping pool, NOT an independent compression ratio 8

sparse_union_lengths_at_context_4096.note: these are CONTEXT-4096-SPECIFIC, not universal context-independent lengths

shape_coverage_required.proxy_vs_gate: random normal/heavy-tail + FP4-grid are SYNTHETIC PROXIES; runtime-captured real-forward tensors + authoritative full-model all-layer parity remain REQUIRED and are NOT met by K=512 pre-gathered microbench

layer_applicability._note: Which layer GATES which op (D4 round 2) — removes the layer-1 vs 'ANY failure' ambiguity. Layer 0 ALWAYS applies. Expected N/A metrics are DISTINCT from missing/failed evaluations.
layer_applicability.continuous_ops: compressor, sinkhorn, combine, sparse -> layer 0 + layer 1
layer_applicability.indexer_logits: layer 0 + layer 2 (selection is the GATE); finite logit-error is a NON-GATING diagnostic unless the user opts it in as an additional gate
layer_applicability.precedence: explicit exceptions (N/A cosine on zero-norm; masked/all-masked N/A) OUTRANK generic metric-completeness; an unexpected nonfinite metric still fails; the BF16-path-vs-global-cosine precedence remains a USER decision

user_decisions_required_by_key.layer1.atol_abs_floor_near_zero_switch: undecided (atol doubles as the near-zero switch; set its positive value)
user_decisions_required_by_key.layer2.topk_set_match: proposed 1.0 (promoted from the layer-2 object to an explicit ratifiable key)
user_decisions_required_by_key.layer2.selected_multiset_tolerance: proposed = tie_eps (the multiset check is the band rule's alternative, not a second gate)
user_decisions_required_by_key.layer2.indexer_logit_error_gating: undecided (selection-only gate, OR selection + an additional non-gating/gating logit-error diagnostic)
user_decisions_required_by_key.bit_exact_per_path: undecided (which NAMED frozen paths, if any, require exact oracle equality; define bit-identity vs numerical-equality incl. signed zero)
user_decisions_required_by_key.metric.zero_and_near_zero_handling: specified structurally (N/A cosine + atol branch); only the atol VALUE is undecided

implementable_without_tolerances: layer-0 hard gates (domain-specific finiteness, shape/dtype/layout, input-domain, determinism-claim recording)
bench + job nonzero-exit propagation verified through the real wrapper (piped logging + final shell commands)
metric STRUCTURE (cosine + abs + rel with named denominator; reject non-finite metrics)
the reference-derived selection/tie evaluation plumbing (minus the ratified numbers)
enforcement_plan: IMPLEMENTED (tolerance-independent): plugin/validate/f4_acceptance.py builds the manifest, runs kernel + the conformed-oracle adapter, enforces layer-0 (shape/dtype/finiteness/REPEATABILITY determinism) + selection (tie_eps=0, reference-owned membership) as HARD gates, collects continuous metrics vs the SCREENING predicate, and exits nonzero on any hard failure. plugin/validate/run_f4_acceptance.sbatch is the fail-closed job wrapper (child nonzero exit -> job nonzero exit; verified). --selftest injects wrong-shape/NaN/duplicate-selection/non-determinism/missing-oracle/below-cutoff faults (all caught) + a correct-kernel no-false-positive. Current run: STATUS=PARTIAL, 0 hard-gate failures; calibration -> results/f4_calibration.json. Layer-1/2 numerical THRESHOLDS remain UNRATIFIED (user), so the gate NEVER returns a full PASS.
calibration_finding: Oracle conformance is decisive (D1): a FP32 indexer oracle induced 7 spurious near-cutoff top-k mismatches; against the BF16-boundary oracle the kernel's induced selection is EXACTLY correct (0 non-tie mismatches, tie_eps=0). All selection gates clean; continuous worst abs-err: combine 0 (bit-exact), sinkhorn ~1e-7, compressor ~6e-6, sparse-scalar ~7e-7, sparse-AMX ~6e-3 (BF16 path, scale-dependent -> NO universal 1e-2). Thresholds to be set per op/path from this evidence, not widened to fit.
